tag: Episode 13 · The Island That Sells Time
title: The Island That Sells Time

beats.t: Sound crossed the water before the boat reached the harbor. Tick, tick. The entire island seemed to sit inside a giant clock.
What's that sound? The whole island's ticking.
Seasickness plus clocks. One star for this island.
One thing before we disembark. This is the Island of Wealth. It will keep asking what you earn, spend, and leave behind.
Wealth means money, right? A money island sounds kind of exciting.
The instant Yeoni stepped onto the pier, a small chime sounded at their wrist. A round clock pattern appeared over pink fur.
[ Island of Wealth · Currency: Time ]  Time held 72:00:00
A clock appeared on my wrist! I mean, foreleg! Anyway, it's there!
Here, you pay in time. Spend it, and your day shrinks by that amount.
Wait. What about time spent cooking? Does that get deducted too?
If somebody buys what you make, it should increase.
Then I'll be the richest one here.
The market bustled. Merchants held out wrists instead of coins when naming prices. Touch wrists together, hear a tick, and the transaction was done.
A blue airship with rabbit ears floated overhead. Papers fluttered like snow from its belly. Short on time? Blue Rabbit Finance will lend you some.
The airship's smiling. Are those ads? It says they'll lend us time.
Borrowed time carries interest. Don't pick those up carelessly.
Small signs stood on every stall. One loaf: 3 minutes. One apple: 5 minutes. Asking directions: 30 seconds.
They charge money for directions? I mean, time?
Smiling must be free, then. Look, nobody's doing it. If it's free, they won't bother.
Before finishing the sentence, Moka claimed an empty stall. He took out his remaining skewer ingredients, lit a fire, and tapped the pot with his ladle.
Authentic Island of Expression skewers! Two minutes each! Not delicious? Three minutes back!
The first customer offered a wrist skeptically. Tick. One bite made the customer's eyes widen. Soon a second wrist extended.
See? Work and your time grows. I'll raise this island to two stars.
That is Direct Wealth. What accumulates from the work of your own hands. Slow, but steady.
Then I can earn some too. I'm good at writing reviews.
Who gives time for reviews? Help manage the line.
The strange thing was people's faces. Many had young voices but white hair. Others had outlines blurred like ink in water.
Yeongnyangi. That person's... face is fading.
They sold too much time. Sell a day, and fade by a day's worth.
Then a basket clattered in the middle of the market.
Thief! someone shouted. The crowd parted like a wave. At its center stood a little white rabbit, clutching a bread basket.
No! I didn't steal it! It's a delivery! My sister baked this bread!
A burly merchant thrust out his wrist. Six loaves, eighteen minutes. There was no transaction record, he said.
The crowd encircled the child. Heard that household went broke lately. Broke family's kid stealing—only natural. Murmurs narrowed the circle.
Wait! The child says it's a delivery! No record doesn't automatically mean theft!
Now the looks turned to the flower pig. A talking pig was apparently not a common sight here either.
Lend me the scales, please. I will weigh the six loaves.
Yeongnyangi placed the bread on one side and the order slip tucked under the basket on the other. The scales stopped perfectly level.
The order slip weighs exactly the same as the bread. I know of no thief who carries an order slip with stolen goods.
The crowd murmured, then dispersed. On this island, nobody disputed proof given by scales.
That was really cool. Five stars.
I said what I saw. Keep the stars.
Thank you! Really, thank you! I'm Luna. I live with my sister at the bakery on that hill!
A bakery? If one loaf sells for three minutes, how many seconds does it cost to make?
Don't know the cost. But my sister doesn't sleep lately. She kneads all night, and every morning her face is a little blurrier.
Yeoni and Yeongnyangi exchanged a look, remembering the faded faces in the market.
Luna. Is your sister selling her time?
I don't know. She says she's fine. She says it ten times a day.
A purple tent stood at the entrance to the bakery alley. A handwritten sign hung above it. Compatibility Readings. Free for Ladies.
You there, the pink lady. Excuse me, but may I have your birth date and time first?
Me? I'm a pig.
Pig or cat, everyone was born at some time. I'll read your compatibility for free.
The man inside looked about twenty-six or twenty-seven. His long hair was loosely tied back. He wore a black glove on his right hand only.
Keep away.
Oh, a guardian. Shall I read yours too, Mr. Cat? There is a charge for gentlemen, though.
Yeongnyangi, are you jealous? Your ears went flat.
Caution. He is suspicious.
Suspicious, yes. He's human but not fading on this island. He's the only sharp one.
Moka was right. Everyone in the market had blurred outlines, but this man was distinct as an ink drawing.
An observant otter. I'll read yours later too.
Don't give an otter a compatibility reading.
My name is Yundal. A fortune-teller here, a guide elsewhere. And you, my lady?
Actually, first—when were you born, Mr. Cat? It costs, but I'll give a first-customer discount.
I don't know.
A cat who doesn't know his own birthday. Apparently I'm not the most suspicious one here.
(Come to think of it, I don't know Yeongnyangi's birthday either.)
Um... July sixth, 2002. Around eight thirty in the morning, I'm told.
With his gloved hand, Yundal took a brush and drew eight boxes on paper. He filled some, then the brush stopped.
A vine born in summer's midday. Eulhae Day Pillar, Byeong-o Month Pillar. But...
Your Hour Pillar is empty. The entire space where your birth hour should be.
[ Year □□ · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □□ ]  4/8
How do you know that? Only we can see it.
I received the same app. Three years ago.
The tent fell quiet. Yeongnyangi's tail struck the floor once.
The same app? You came to mend your destiny too?
Came to mend it, ended up staying. Call me your senior user.
One piece of free advice. People with empty Hour Pillars sell for the highest price here. There is an empty slot in which to hold time.
Sell? Who would buy me?
There is always a buyer. The question is who sets the price first.
Yundal folded the paper and handed it to Yeoni. Beside the Hour Pillar, small letters read: Just like me.
(What does 'like me' mean?)
Compatibility booth review. Free, but somehow felt expensive. Three stars.
Three stars is this tent's all-time high. Usually it's one.
The bakery at the hilltop was small and old. Through the windows, a city above the clouds spread below. Opening the door released the smell of fresh bread. Moka's nose twitched.
That smell is... real. The first real smell I've found on this island.
You brought Luna home. Thank you. Have a loaf each. No charge.
Free? On this island?
If I charge time for bread, it starts tasting like a clock.
Luna's sister's face was half-faded. Only her flour-dusted fingertips were strangely clear.
Good dough texture. Honest hands. But when do you sleep?
The orders are backed up. I have to prepare tomorrow morning's too.
You're lying. You didn't sleep yesterday either.
I can't take free bread. Let me work instead. I'm good at folding dough.
With pig hooves?
Pig hooves are made for dough. They're soft.
Then... twelve minutes per hour. Starting tomorrow morning.
Luna's sister lightly touched her wrist to Yeoni's hoof. Tick. Small words appeared beside the numbers. Scheduled wages: 12 minutes.
My first salary... I mean, hourly wage.
A document stuck out beneath the counter. A contract stamped with a blue rabbit. Yeoni narrowed their eyes.
(Blue Rabbit Finance... a time-loan contract?)
Then the ticking in Yeoni's hoof accelerated. The numbers on the clock mark began draining away by themselves.
Yeongnyangi! My time's shrinking! I haven't bought anything!
Someone is collecting it. Look at the end of that thread.
A fine black thread extended from Yeoni's hoof through the window. It vanished downhill toward the clock tower rising at the island's center.
Something's on top of the tower.
A black silhouette sat on a clock hand at the top. A cloak hem blew in the wind.
That cloak... the tiger.
Yeongnyangi stepped in front of Yeoni. The black thread pulled taut. The numbers kept falling.
Then the bakery door opened. The man from the purple tent stood there, breathing hard, pulling off his right glove with his teeth.
Sooner than I expected. My lady, promise one thing before I cut that thread. Don't be hurt if tomorrow I forget what you see now.
